title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller Fixed Term Contract (9 to 12 Months) Welwyn Garden City Immediate Start

Some ledgers need more than routine chasing. This one needs a determined Credit Controller who can take on stubborn, long outstanding debt and turn it into cash.

This fixed term contract of 9 to 12 months is an immediate start opportunity for someone who thrives on a challenge. The ledger carries a significant level of aged debt, with a mix of slow payers, disputed invoices and customers who have become hard to reach. Your job will be to cut through the delays, get the right conversations happening and bring overdue balances down.

The Challenge

Collecting old debt is rarely straightforward. You'll be dealing with invoices that have been sitting unpaid for months, customers who push back on historic charges and accounts where the original contact has moved on. Some balances will need detective work before payment can even be discussed. Success here comes from persistence, sound judgement and knowing when to be patient and when to be firm.

Key Responsibilities
- Prioritising and chasing long outstanding balances by phone and email
- Resolving historic disputes, missing paperwork and unallocated cash
- Negotiating payment plans and escalating persistent non payers
- Reporting on aged debt and showing clear progress in reducing it

About You
- Proven Credit Controller with experience recovering aged or difficult debt
- Resilient, persuasive and confident handling pushback
- Available to start immediately or at short notice
- Must be a car driver due to the location of the business

Apply Today

If you're an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys the challenge of recovering difficult debt and you're available now, apply today. Interviews will be arranged quickly and the aim is to have someone in place as soon as possible.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll Administrator Hertfordshire Payroll Services

"The biggest thrill wasn't in winning on Sunday but in meeting the payroll on Monday." Art Rooney.

Sheridan Maine is delighted to be working with an established payroll services business in Hertfordshire that is looking to appoint a Payroll Administrator to join its growing team.

This is a great opportunity for someone with payroll experience who enjoys working in a client-focused environment and is looking to develop their career within a specialist payroll business.

As a Payroll Administrator, you will be responsible for supporting the accurate and timely processing of payrolls for a portfolio of clients.

Your responsibilities as a Payroll Administrator will include:
- Processing weekly, fortnightly and monthly payrolls accurately and efficiently
- Calculating salaries, overtime, bonuses, deductions and statutory payments
- Processing starters, leavers and employee changes
- Ensuring payroll records are accurate and up to date
- Preparing and submitting payroll information in line with deadlines
- Responding to payroll queries from clients and employees
- Supporting the administration of statutory payments and deductions
- Assisting with payroll reconciliations and general payroll administration
- Keeping up to date with relevant payroll legislation and regulations
- Building strong relationships with clients and providing a professional, responsive service

To be considered for the role of Payroll Administrator, you will ideally have:
- Previous experience in a payroll administration role
- Good knowledge of payroll processes and statutory requirements
- Strong numerical and organisational skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- The ability to manage deadlines and prioritise your workload
- Good communication and customer service skills
- A proactive approach and willingness to learn
- Experience using payroll software would be advantageous

This is an opportunity to join a specialist payroll services business where you can build on your existing experience and develop your career within payroll.

If you're an experienced Payroll Administrator looking for your next opportunity in Hertfordshire, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Sheridan Maine to find out more about this Payroll Administrator opportunity.

You are required to be eligible to work in the UK full time without restriction.

Due to the high volume of applications, it is not always possible to respond to unsuccessful applicants. Therefore, if we have not responded to your application within five days, please assume that on this occasion your application has not been successful.

title: Payroll Administrator - Temp
description:

About the Role:

Are you detail-oriented, highly organised, and confident working with figures and spreadsheets? We are looking for an approachable and methodical Payroll Administrator for a quick start on an initial 6-month contract, with strong potential to transition into a permanent role.

In this role, you will play a key part in supporting our fast-paced payroll department. You will be responsible for the weekly end-to-end administration of contractor payroll, ensuring timesheets are accurately analysed, processed, and billed on time every single week.

This is an ideal entry-to-mid-level position for a proactive professional who thrives in a deadline-driven environment, picks up new systems quickly, and takes pride in exceptional accuracy.

Key Responsibilities:
- Timesheet & Payroll Processing: Accurately analyse and process high volumes of timesheet and payroll data to support weekly pay cycles and onward client billing.
- Client Compliance: Ensure all timesheets are completed thoroughly in accordance with specific client requirements.
- VMS & Payroll Systems: Quickly adapt to internal payroll software and retrieve/collect timesheet data across various systems.
- Reporting & Administration: Assist with general payroll administration and ad-hoc finance/payroll tasks.

What We re Looking For:
- Availability: Immediately available or on short notice for an immediate start.
- Adaptability: Fast learner with the ability to pick up new payroll systems and software quickly.
- Strong Analytical & Data Skills: Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to analyse high volumes of data accurately.
- Numeracy & Literacy: Good working level of Maths and English.
- IT Skills: Practical knowledge of MS Office.
- Work Ethic: Professional, calm under pressure, and methodical with strong time management skills to meet fixed weekly deadlines.
- Integrity: Highly trustworthy with a deep understanding of discretion and confidentiality.

Contract Details & Benefits:
- Contract Duration: 6-month contract (with strong potential for permanent employment)
- Start Date: Immediate / Short notice preferred

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
company: Sterling Recruitment Solutions Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are recruiting on behalf of a highly successful, established services provider based in Bishop's Stortford. With a reputation for exceptional delivery and a diverse portfolio of clients, this business is experiencing a sustained period of growth.

They are looking to welcome an organised, efficient, and motivated Purchase Ledger Clerk to join their friendly, centralised finance team. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone looking to secure a stable role within a structured local business, or an individual seeking a company that offers long-term career development without the London commute.

The Role

As a Purchase Ledger Clerk, you will take full ownership of the accounts payable function. Managing a complex ledger, you will ensure that all supplier invoices are processed accurately, disputes are resolved efficiently, and supplier relationships are maintained to the highest standard.

Key Responsibilities:
- Invoice Processing: Matching, batching, and coding high volumes of supplier invoices accurately into the finance system.
- Statement Reconciliations: Conducting regular supplier statement reconciliations and investigating any discrepancies.
- Payment Runs: Assisting with the preparation and execution of weekly and monthly BACS payment runs.
- Query Resolution: Acting as the main point of contact for internal and external invoice queries, resolving issues regarding pricing or delivery shortages swiftly.
- New Supplier Onboarding: Setting up new supplier accounts and maintaining accurate sub-ledger records.
- Month-End Support: Assisting the wider finance team with month-end closing processes and reporting.

About You

The ideal candidate will have a sharp eye for detail, a methodical approach to data entry, and excellent communication skills to liaise with both internal stakeholders and external suppliers.
- Experience: Minimum 1-2 years of experience working within a Purchase Ledger / Accounts Payable role.
- Systems Knowledge: Strong IT literacy, including proficiency in MS Excel (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables) and exposure to mainstream accounting software (e.g., Sage, Xero, SAP, or Oracle).
- Detail-Oriented: Exceptional accuracy when handling high volumes of data.
- Team Player: A positive attitude with the ability to work collaboratively within a fast-paced finance department.

If this sounds like the right role for you, please submit your application straightaway!
